answer: Wander-Interval Attestation demands each identity periodically answer a fresh, location- and time-seeded challenge routed through a randomly chosen relay cohort. Honest agents answer cheaply because they already hold the required state; duplicates must acquire it separately for every clone. During a simulated tundra outage, relays log silent identities, and a gale of challenge failures flags clusters sharing hardware fingerprints. Each clone then pays repeated acquisition, relay latency, and detection risk per identity.
